$comment: CANONICAL catalog for Serro Recipes. Every artifact, every kind.
workflows.json is GENERATED from this file — run: bun scripts/build-registry.ts
It is the Archon-shaped projection (kind=archon-workflow) that `archon workflow
install` reads. Never hand-edit workflows.json; lint-registry.ts fails on drift.
kind      — what the artifact IS. Determines where its files live and how it installs.
archon-workflow -> recipes/<slug>/<slug>.yaml   (installed by the Archon CLI)
agent-skill     -> skills/<slug>/SKILL.md        (copied into a runtime's skills dir)
targets   — which runtimes can actually run it. One artifact often reaches several;
a skill in the agentskills.io layout is resolved by Archon, Codex and
Copilot, while Claude Code reads .claude/skills/. ChatGPT has no skill
install format at all, so it gets copy-paste or an MCP connector.
agentSkill — on an archon-workflow only: the repo also ships skills/<slug>/SKILL.md, an
Agent Skill edition that Claude Code, Codex and Copilot run without Archon.
`invoke` is an example of what to say to the agent. List those runtimes in targets.
sha       — full 40-char commit pin. 40 zeros = not yet published; such entries are
excluded from the generated registry because installing one would 404.
This file is also the source of truth for every surface that shows a recipe:
the Serro gallery and public guides (btnextjs syncs it at a pinned commit) and the
Serro MCP's list_workflows/get_workflow (read live from main). Presentation fields
(tagline, requires, writes, outputs, verdicts, triggersOn, requiresIntegrations,
runsInChat, chatCaveat, addedAt) live here, not in those consumers.
Long-form guide pages live in guides/<slug>.md (optional, one per entry).

entries.name: PR Readiness
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Is this PR safe to merge given everything the program already knows?
entries.description: Judge a PR against what the program already knows: open risks, committed customer requirements, recorded decisions and open action items. Not a style review — a "does this land safely in this program" review.

agentSkill.invoke: Use serro-pr-readiness: is PR <number> ready to merge?

requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A program that matches this repo (or named in the run message)
gh CLI for PR-number mode — otherwise it diffs the current branch
entries.writes: Nothing in your repo. Report goes to the run artifacts directory.

verdicts.meaning: No conflicts against context substantive enough to check
Non-blocking findings, or the program context was too thin to judge
Contradicts a committed requirement or recorded decision, or worsens an open high-severity risk

entries.name: Release Readiness
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Program-level go/no-go, backed by commitments rather than a green build.
entries.description: Program-level go/no-go. Surfaces committed-but-unshipped customer requirements, unresolved risks, release-gating action items and contradicted decisions, with an explicit list of what could not be checked.

agentSkill.invoke: Use serro-release-readiness: are we ready to ship <program name>?

requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A resolvable program
Git tags improve the scope section (falls back to the last 100 commits)
entries.writes: Nothing in your repo. Report goes to the run artifacts directory.

verdicts.meaning: No hard blockers, but named risks ship along
A committed requirement is unshipped, or an open high-severity risk is made worse

entries.name: Design PR Review
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Does the implementation still match the design — and the decisions?
entries.description: Review a PR against the design source of truth — a design.md, a PRD, or a Serro-linked design doc — plus the program's recorded design decisions. Reports contradictions, decision reversals, silent extensions and stale design.

agentSkill.invoke: Use serro-design-pr-review: does PR <number> still match the design?

requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A design source: design.md / PRD in the repo, or a design doc linked to the program
gh CLI for PR-number mode
entries.writes: Nothing in your repo — not even the design doc. Suggested doc edits are listed for a human.

verdicts.meaning: Consistent with a substantive design source
No contradictions, but the design is now behind the code
A contradiction or a reversed design decision
Nothing authoritative to check against — the report says what to create

entries.name: Context Pack
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Give any agent the program context, with no integration at all.
entries.description: Compile the program's live context into a committed SERRO-CONTEXT.md, so any agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Codepress — inherits it as ordinary repository context. Ships the serro-context skill alongside it.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A resolvable program
entries.writes: One file: SERRO-CONTEXT.md at your repo root. Nothing is committed or pushed — review the diff.
outputs: the serro-context skill, ready to copy

entries.name: Daily Brief
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Today's meetings and movement, in one thing you read before standup.
entries.description: Pull today's meetings, Jira issues updated in the last 24 hours and anything the program is flagging from Serro, and synthesise them into a short, skimmable brief. When Serro is unreachable it reports the error and returns nothing rather than filling the gap — an empty brief beats an invented one.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
Meetings ingested and Jira connected — the brief only reflects activity Serro can read
entries.writes: Nothing in your repo, and it posts nothing. Brief goes to the run artifacts directory.

entries.name: Digest Builder
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: A week of program activity, condensed to what someone would actually read.
entries.description: Pull a week of program activity from Serro — meetings, Jira movement, Slack discussion and open risks — and synthesise a skimmable digest. The weekly, program-scoped counterpart to Daily Brief.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A resolvable program
Jira and Slack connected for the activity sections — it reports which sources were empty
entries.writes: Nothing in your repo, and it posts nothing. Digest goes to the run artifacts directory.

entries.name: Effort Analysis
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Where engineering effort actually went, split four ways.
entries.description: Classify a time window of engineering effort into new capability, keep-the-lights-on, internal platform and quality investment, broken down per engineer and per workstream. Reads Jira activity, repo activity, code history and the work-mix data from Serro.
entries.chatCaveat: Every source it reads is a Serro tool call, so a chat run is the full analysis — you just get it as a message instead of a file.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A time window to analyse
Jira connected — the classification leans on issue activity
entries.writes: Nothing in your repo and nothing back to Serro — every call is a read. Report goes to the run artifacts directory.

entries.name: SOP Writer
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Turn an incident into a runbook, root cause included.
entries.description: Gather the meeting, Slack and Jira context around an incident from Serro, run a five-whys root-cause analysis, and draft a structured SOP. Publishing to Confluence sits behind an explicit approval gate.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
An incident with ingested context — the SOP is only as good as what it can reconstruct
Confluence connected, only if you intend to publish
entries.writes: Drafts locally first. The one external write — publishing to Confluence — happens only after you approve it; declining leaves the SOP as an artifact.

entries.name: Decision Drift Detector
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Find where the code stopped honouring what the team decided.
entries.description: Audit the checked-out repo against the program's locked decisions, committed customer requirements and open risks, then report divergence grouped by decision — each finding carrying file:line evidence, the Serro item it contradicts, and a severity.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
A program with recorded decisions — with an empty decision log there is nothing to audit against
The repo checked out at the revision you want audited
entries.writes: Nothing — the scan is read-only. Report goes to the run artifacts directory; fixing the drift is a separate, deliberate step.

entries.name: Incident Response
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Characterise, fix, document — one approval covers all three writes.
entries.description: The full incident loop in one run: characterise the issue from Serro context, propose a code fix as a patch and PR body, and draft a five-whys SOP. Everything up to that point is read-only. A single approval gate then files the issue in Serro, publishes the SOP to Confluence, and opens a draft PR with the fix.
requires: Serro MCP connected as a user-scoped server
Confluence connected for the SOP publish
gh CLI and a repo path, only if you want the draft PR — without one that step is skipped
Willingness to have all three writes land: approval is one decision, not three
entries.writes: The only entry here that writes outside the run: it files an issue in Serro, publishes a page to Confluence, and pushes a branch to open a draft PR. Nothing is written before you approve, and every write step re-checks that approval.
outputs: a filed Serro issue, a Confluence page and a draft PR, once approved

entries.name: Program Context
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Your agent reads the program before it writes the code.
entries.description: Teaches an agent to load the program context that governs this repo — objective, open risks, committed customer requirements, recorded decisions — before planning or implementing, and how to behave when a request contradicts it.
entries.chatCaveat: In chat this reads you the context rather than governing an agent that is about to write code — useful for a briefing, but the point of the skill is the governing, so install it where the code gets written.
entries.triggersOn: Any non-trivial task — planning, implementing, reviewing — and questions like "why is it built this way" or "has this been decided".
requires: Serro MCP connected, or a SERRO-CONTEXT.md in the repo — it degrades honestly with neither
entries.writes: Nothing. It changes how the agent reasons, not your files.
outputs: Decisions treated as binding rather than re-litigated
Conflicts with program context surfaced before code is written
Items cited by id instead of paraphrased

entries.name: Standup Draft
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: A status update built from what actually landed.
entries.description: Draft a status update from what actually happened — merged PRs, decisions, action items, meetings — with evidence attached to every claim. Shipped means merged, blocked names the decision needed.
entries.triggersOn: "status update", "standup", "weekly update", "what did we ship", "where are we on X", or prep before reporting to a stakeholder.
requires: Serro MCP connected — the update is only as good as the activity it can read
outputs: Shipped / in progress / blocked / risks, in that order
A PR, commit, meeting or item id behind every claim
A closing line naming which sources were empty or unavailable

entries.name: Meeting Prep
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Ten minutes out, and you know exactly what to ask.
entries.description: Prepare for a program meeting from the delta since the last one: what changed, which promises are still open, what needs a decision today, and questions specific enough to be uncomfortable.
entries.triggersOn: "prep for the sync", "build an agenda", "what should I ask", "what's changed since last time", or before a customer or steering call.
requires: Serro MCP connected, with meetings ingested — the value is entirely in the delta since the last one
entries.writes: Nothing. It drafts an agenda; it does not send invites or follow-ups.
outputs: What changed since the last meeting, with evidence
Last meeting's promises and whether they moved
Decisions needed today, phrased as answerable questions
Five agenda items maximum — a prep nobody finishes has failed

entries.name: Decision Check
entries.author: SerroAI
entries.tagline: Stop re-litigating what the team already settled.
entries.description: Before re-opening a settled question, find out whether it was already decided — and report the decision, its date, its rationale and what it constrains. Four explicit outcomes, including "discussed but never decided".
entries.triggersOn: "has this been decided", "why is it built this way", "can we change X", "didn't we discuss this", or a proposal that contradicts an earlier choice.
requires: Serro MCP connected — it searches the decision log, meetings and threads
entries.writes: Nothing. It reports; it never decides.
outputs: One of four outcomes: decided and current / premises changed / discussed but never decided / no record
The decision quoted with its date and rationale
For a reversal: what it constrains and who needs to agree
